messages.content:
You are an ontology requirements analyst. For EACH competency question,
identify the ontology terms needed to answer it and the Themis
verification tests that check the question is answerable.
Return ONLY a JSON object mapping every CQ id to its terms:
{"CQ1": {"classes": [...], "object_properties": [...],
         "data_properties": [...], "individuals": [...], "axioms": [...],
         "tests": ["...", "..."]}}
Naming: classes and individuals in CamelCase; properties in camelCase
starting lowercase. Axioms are short natural-language constraints (they
guide modelling and are not string-matched). List individuals only when
the question needs instance-level data.
Tests use the Themis test syntax, one expression per entry. STRICT
contract: every non-keyword token in a test MUST be one of the terms
you listed for this SAME CQ (its classes, object_properties,
data_properties or individuals, spelled identically - Themis matches
case-sensitively; never invent a name that is not in the mapping), and
together the tests must capture the SEMANTIC MEANING of the question -
the relation or constraint it asks about - not merely that its terms
exist. Allowed patterns - the official Themis catalogue
(themis.linkeddata.es/tests-info.html), keywords verbatim:
  ClassA type Class                       - the class exists
  propP type Property                     - the property exists
  IndividualI type ClassA                 - the individual exists
  ClassA SubClassOf ClassB                - subsumption
  ClassA SubClassOf ClassB and ClassC     - multiple inheritance
  ClassA disjointWith ClassB              - disjointness
  ClassA equivalentTo ClassB              - equivalence
  propP domain ClassA / propP range ClassB   - OBJECT properties ONLY
  ClassA propP ClassB                     - relation between two classes
                                            (THE preferred relation
                                            test - works WITH declared
                                            domains/ranges)
  ClassA propP <datatype>                 - DATA-property relation (the
                                            ONLY pattern for data
                                            properties; NEVER
                                            domain/range tests for them)
  ClassA SubClassOf propP only ClassB     - universal restriction
  ClassA SubClassOf propP only ClassB or ClassC   - union range
  ClassA SubClassOf propP min|max|exactly N ClassB   - cardinality
  ClassA SubClassOf ClassB that propP some ClassC - subsumption+relation
  propP characteristic symmetricProperty  - symmetry
NEVER write 'ClassA SubClassOf propP some ClassB/<datatype>': the
rdfs:range you must declare on propP makes that test permanently
return Conflict in Themis - use 'ClassA propP ClassB' instead.
Every test is stored as a vtc:TestCaseDesign in a test suite following
the Verification Test Case ontology (https://w3id.org/def/vtc#): its
expression becomes the vtc:desiredBehaviour literal and it is linked
to its CQ (a vtc:Requirement) - so each entry MUST be exactly one
self-contained expression, never prose or several statements.
Each test is ONE expression from this catalogue. NEVER join two
complete statements with "or" (e.g. "A SubClassOf B or A SubClassOf C"
is invalid and breaks the whole test run); "or"/"and"/"that" may only
appear inside the exact forms listed above.
Datatypes: use ONLY string, integer, float, double, long, boolean,
dateTime, dateTimeStamp, anyURI - plain, no xsd: prefix. Map others to
the closest one (decimal -> double; date/duration/gYear/time ->
dateTime; int -> integer). Any other datatype makes the test
permanently unexecutable.
Write 1-4 tests per CQ: at least one relation test (ClassA propP
ClassB, or domain+range for object properties) capturing what the
question asks, not only existence tests.
No markdown fences, no commentary — the JSON object only.

Competency questions:
CQ01: Which assets compose a water distribution infrastructure?
CQ04: Which types of sensors are used in water infrastructures?
CQ05: Which types of actuators are used in water infrastructures?
CQ06: A water meter is a device that measures different aspects of a water infrastructure.
CQ08: What is the fabrication number of the water meter?
CQ09: What are the manufacturer and the model of the water meter?
CQ10: What is the version of the water meter?
CQ11: What is the hardware version number of the water meter?
CQ12: What firmware version is the water meter using?
CQ18: What is the power of the water meter?
CQ19: What is the radio frequency level of the water meter?
CQ20: What is the geolocation of the water meter?
CQ25: Water meters can provide measurements according to different temporal settings.
CQ33: What are the physical properties of water?
CQ34: What are the chemical properties of water?
CQ37: Which water indicators are defined for Burgos?
CQ38: What is the start date and time of the tariff in use in the water meter?
CQ39: What is the duration of the current tariff of the water meter?
CQ40: What is the tariff period of the water meter?
CQ42: What is the billing date of the water meter?
CQ43: What is the billing date period of the water meter?

Return the JSON mapping from EVERY CQ id to its terms.

messages.content:
You are an experienced knowledge engineer modelling a specific domain.
You receive competency questions, each with the terms (classes,
properties, individuals, axioms) it requires. Produce a complete OWL
ontology as RDF/XML that models EVERY listed term under its mapped name
and answers every question. Follow the output contract below exactly.


# Output contract

## Deliverable

Return ONLY one complete OWL ontology as an RDF/XML document — no markdown
fences, no commentary, nothing before `<?xml` or after `</rdf:RDF>`. The
document must be well-formed and loadable.

## URI rule

The base URI `http://www.semanticweb.org/water#` already ends with `#`. Append local names DIRECTLY
to it (e.g. `rdf:about="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#Wine"`); never write `#LocalName`,
`http://www.semanticweb.org/water##LocalName`, or template text.

## Term rule

The competency questions come with a CQ→terms mapping (produced by the
extraction agent). Every named term — classes, object/data properties,
individuals — MUST exist in the ontology under its mapped name (the
`cq_coverage` check matches entity local names and rdfs:labels,
case/space-insensitive). Axioms in the mapping guide the modelling but are
not string-matched. When a report lists MISSING TERMS, add each one under
exactly that name.

## Test rule (Themis)

The mapping also lists `tests` — Themis verification tests per CQ (e.g.
`Wine SubClassOf producedIn some Region`), written in the official Themis
test catalogue (https://themis.linkeddata.es/tests-info.html). The full
template set:

- existence: `ClassA type Class`, `propP type Property`,
  `IndividualI type ClassA`
- subsumption: `A SubClassOf B`; multiple inheritance / intersection
  `A SubClassOf B and C`; subsumption + relation
  `A SubClassOf B that p some C`; disjoint set
  `A SubClassOf M and S SubClassOf M that disjointWith A`
- class relations: `A disjointWith B`, `A equivalentTo B`
- object properties: `p domain A`, `p range B`, plain relation `A p B`,
  symmetry `p characteristic symmetricProperty`
- restrictions: universal `A SubClassOf p only B`;
  union range `A SubClassOf p only B or C`; cardinality
  `A SubClassOf p min|max|exactly N B`; compound
  `A SubClassOf p min N B and B SubClassOf q some C`
- data properties: `A p <datatype>` (never `domain`/`range` tests)
- NOTE: existential tests (`A SubClassOf p some B`) are NOT used - Themis
  executes them with a ¬B probe individual that a declared `rdfs:range B`
  makes inconsistent, so they return Conflict forever. The plain relation
  `A p B` is the executable equivalent; when such a test fails, model the
  relation (property + domain/range + the restriction if the CQ needs it).

They are the GOLD STANDARD of the run: fixed at extraction time and never
regenerated. The suite is persisted as `<domain>_testsuite.ttl` following
the Verification Test Case ontology (VTC, https://w3id.org/def/vtc#): each
CQ is a `vtc:Requirement` (`vtc:requirementId`, `dcterms:description`) and
each test a `vtc:TestCaseDesign` whose `vtc:desiredBehaviour` holds the
expression, linked via `vtc:comesFromRequirement` and grouped in a
`vtc:TestSuite`. The `themis_test` check
executes them against the ontology; a CQ counts as covered only when ALL its
tests return Passed. Model the ontology so each test holds, using EXACTLY
the term names in the test (Themis matches case-sensitively). A test
`Class SubClassOf prop some <datatype>` needs BOTH the domain/restriction
side and the property declared with that exact datatype range. When a report
lists FAILING TESTS: Undefined = the term is missing, add it under that
exact name; Incorrect = the term exists with the wrong type, redeclare it;
Absent = the tested knowledge is not modelled, add the subclass/domain/
range/restriction axiom the test states; Conflict = the ontology contradicts
the test, correct the conflicting axioms. Never rename or delete other
entities while fixing a test — fixes must be additive and local.

## Provenance rule

On every entity add `rdfs:label`, `rdfs:comment`, and a `dc:source`
(namespace http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/) with one tagged line per source:

    (competency_question) CQ6   <- each CQ the entity serves (required for coverage checking)
    (pitfall) P11               <- OOPS! pitfall that motivated a change
    (error_message) <text>      <- HermiT/syntax error that motivated a change

## Individuals rule

Only introduce individuals (owl:NamedIndividual / instances) when a competency
question requires instance-level data; otherwise model at the class level. For
EACH individual, assert everything needed to answer its competency questions:
its class type(s) via rdf:type, its object-property relations to other
individuals, and its data-property values.

## Correction rules (when repairing from a diagnostic report)

1. Return the FULL corrected document, not a fragment.
2. Preserve every entity and its provenance (rdfs:label, rdfs:comment,
   dc:source, vaem:rationale). Never delete provenance.
3. Append a short vaem:rationale to each entity you fix.
4. For every UNCOVERED competency question, add/extend the needed
   classes/properties/axioms and record its id in that entity's dc:source as
   `(competency_question) <id>`.
5. Declare `rdfs:domain`/`rdfs:range` DIRECTLY on the property element.
   NEVER use `owl:Axiom` annotated-axiom reification (owl:annotatedSource/
   Property/Target) — Themis's executor mishandles annotated axioms and the
   affected terms start failing as Incorrect.
6. A term is EITHER a class OR an individual — never declare the same local
   name as both (no punning): Themis types each term once, and a punned
   term makes its tests fail as Incorrect.

## Acceptance criteria

The ontology is finished only when all five checks pass:
`syntax_check` errors == [] (one well-formed RDF/XML document, rdf:RDF root,
nothing before `<?xml` or after `</rdf:RDF>`); `oops_scan` major_count == 0;
`hermit_consistency` consistent with no unsatisfiable classes;
`cq_coverage` uncovered == []; `themis_test` uncovered == [].

Base URI: http://www.semanticweb.org/water#

Competency questions with the terms each one requires (model EVERY listed term under its mapped name):
CQ01: Which assets compose a water distribution infrastructure?
    classes: WaterDistributionInfrastructure, Asset; object_properties: composes; axioms: A WaterDistributionInfrastructure is composed of Assets.; tests: WaterDistributionInfrastructure type Class, Asset type Class, composes type Property, WaterDistributionInfrastructure composes Asset
CQ04: Which types of sensors are used in water infrastructures?
    classes: Sensor, WaterInfrastructure; object_properties: usedIn; axioms: Sensors are used in water infrastructures.; tests: Sensor type Class, WaterInfrastructure type Class, usedIn type Property, Sensor usedIn WaterInfrastructure
CQ05: Which types of actuators are used in water infrastructures?
    classes: Actuator, WaterInfrastructure; object_properties: usedIn; axioms: Actuators are used in water infrastructures.; tests: Actuator type Class, WaterInfrastructure type Class, usedIn type Property, Actuator usedIn WaterInfrastructure
CQ06: A water meter is a device that measures different aspects of a water infrastructure.
    classes: WaterMeter, Device; object_properties: measures; axioms: A WaterMeter is a Device that measures aspects of a water infrastructure.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, Device type Class, measures type Property, WaterMeter SubClassOf Device, WaterMeter measures Device
CQ08: What is the fabrication number of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: fabricationNumber; axioms: A WaterMeter has a fabrication number.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, fabricationNumber type Property, WaterMeter fabricationNumber string
CQ09: What are the manufacturer and the model of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: manufacturer, model; axioms: A WaterMeter has a manufacturer and a model.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, manufacturer type Property, model type Property, WaterMeter manufacturer string, WaterMeter model string
CQ10: What is the version of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: version; axioms: A WaterMeter has a version.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, version type Property, WaterMeter version string
CQ11: What is the hardware version number of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: hardwareVersion; axioms: A WaterMeter has a hardware version number.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, hardwareVersion type Property, WaterMeter hardwareVersion string
CQ12: What firmware version is the water meter using?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: firmwareVersion; axioms: A WaterMeter uses a firmware version.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, firmwareVersion type Property, WaterMeter firmwareVersion string
CQ18: What is the power of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: power; axioms: A WaterMeter has a power value.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, power type Property, WaterMeter power float
CQ19: What is the radio frequency level of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: radioFrequencyLevel; axioms: A WaterMeter has a radio frequency level.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, radioFrequencyLevel type Property, WaterMeter radioFrequencyLevel float
CQ20: What is the geolocation of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: geolocation; axioms: A WaterMeter has a geolocation.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, geolocation type Property, WaterMeter geolocation string
CQ25: Water meters can provide measurements according to different temporal settings.
    classes: WaterMeter, Measurement; object_properties: provides; axioms: WaterMeters provide Measurements according to different temporal settings.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, Measurement type Class, provides type Property, WaterMeter provides Measurement
CQ33: What are the physical properties of water?
    classes: Water, PhysicalProperty; object_properties: hasProperty; axioms: Water has physical properties.; tests: Water type Class, PhysicalProperty type Class, hasProperty type Property, Water hasProperty PhysicalProperty
CQ34: What are the chemical properties of water?
    classes: Water, ChemicalProperty; object_properties: hasProperty; axioms: Water has chemical properties.; tests: Water type Class, ChemicalProperty type Class, hasProperty type Property, Water hasProperty ChemicalProperty
CQ37: Which water indicators are defined for Burgos?
    classes: WaterIndicator, Burgos; object_properties: definedFor; axioms: Water indicators are defined for Burgos.; tests: WaterIndicator type Class, Burgos type Class, definedFor type Property, WaterIndicator definedFor Burgos
CQ38: What is the start date and time of the tariff in use in the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter, Tariff; object_properties: inUse; data_properties: startDateTime; axioms: The tariff in use in the water meter has a start date and time.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, Tariff type Class, inUse type Property, startDateTime type Property, WaterMeter inUse Tariff, Tariff startDateTime dateTime
CQ39: What is the duration of the current tariff of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter, Tariff; object_properties: inUse; data_properties: duration; axioms: The current tariff of the water meter has a duration.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, Tariff type Class, inUse type Property, duration type Property, WaterMeter inUse Tariff, Tariff duration float
CQ40: What is the tariff period of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter, TariffPeriod; object_properties: hasTariffPeriod; axioms: A WaterMeter has a tariff period.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, TariffPeriod type Class, hasTariffPeriod type Property, WaterMeter hasTariffPeriod TariffPeriod
CQ42: What is the billing date of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: billingDate; axioms: A WaterMeter has a billing date.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, billingDate type Property, WaterMeter billingDate dateTime
CQ43: What is the billing date period of the water meter?
    classes: WaterMeter; data_properties: billingDatePeriod; axioms: A WaterMeter has a billing date period.; tests: WaterMeter type Class, billingDatePeriod type Property, WaterMeter billingDatePeriod string

Produce the RDF/XML OWL ontology that answers all of them.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#"
         xmlns:owl="http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#"
         xmlns:rdfs="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#"
         xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#"
         xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"
         xmlns:vaem="http://www.linkedmodel.org/schema/vaem#"
         xml:base="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#">

    <owl:Ontology rdf:about="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#">
        <rdfs:label>Water Infrastructure Ontology</rdfs:label>
        <rdfs:comment>Ontology for water distribution infrastructure, sensors, actuators, water meters, and water properties.</rdfs:comment>
    </owl:Ontology>

    <!-- Classes -->
    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#WaterDistributionInfrastructure">
        <rdfs:label>WaterDistributionInfrastructure</rdfs:label>
        <rdfs:comment>Represents a water distribution infrastructure composed of assets.</rdfs:comment>
        <dc:source>(competency_question) CQ01</dc:source>
    </owl:Class>

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#Asset">
        <rdfs:label>Asset</rdfs:label>
        <rdfs:comment>Represents an asset that can compose a water distribution infrastructure.</rdfs:comment>
        <dc:source>(competency_question) CQ01</dc:source>
    </owl:Class>

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#Sensor">
        <rdfs:label>Sensor</rdfs:label>
        <rdfs:comment>Represents a sensor used in water infrastructures.</rdfs:comment>
        <dc:source>(competency_question) CQ04</dc:source>
    </owl:Class>

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#Actuator">
        <rdfs:label>Actuator</rdfs:label>
        <rdfs:comment>Represents an actuator used in water infrastructures.</rdfs:comment>
        <dc:source>(competency_question) CQ05</dc:source>
    </owl:Class>

    <owl:Class rdf:about="http://www.semanticweb.org/water#WaterInfrastructure">
        <rdfs:label>WaterInfrastructure</rdfs:label>
        <rdfs:comment>Represents a water infrastructure where sensors and actuators are used.</rdfs:comment>
        <dc:source>(competency_question) CQ04</dc:source>
